appendix.title: Greek & Roman Mythology · Reference Table
rows: Hephaestus discovers Aphrodite’s affair with Ares.
Aeneas escapes Troy and settles in Italy; Rome is later founded by Romulus.
Zeus carries Europa to Crete in the form of a bull.
Zeus swallows Metis; Athena is later born from his head.
Zeus is king of the gods; Ares is the son of Zeus and Hera.
In Hesiod’s account, Hera bears Hephaestus without Zeus.
Hermes, the messenger of the gods, is the son of Zeus and Maia.
Horae (goddesses of the seasons and order)
Thetis is a sea nymph (Nereid) and the mother of Achilles.
The golden apple of discord and the Judgment of Paris.
Helen’s departure with Paris is central to the myth of the Trojan War.
Hera is Hephaestus’s mother; some accounts name Zeus as his father, while Hesiod names no father.
